newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African police storm hostage jail cell, one dead.
newsitem.headline: S.African police storm hostage jail cell, one dead.

text.p: One prisoner was killed and several were wounded on Wednesday when police and warders stormed cells where one of South Africa's most notorious criminals was holding five hostages, a prison spokesman said.

Thembesile "Tyson" Makaluza, who had taken three prison employees and two electricians hostage since Monday in a bid to escape from St Albans prison near the Indian Ocean city of Port Elizabeth, was one of those wounded in the attack.
Prisons spokesman Bert Slabbert said the hostages were released unharmed after police and warders attacked the cells where they were held at 3 a.m.
"The hostages are unharmed but one prisoner was shot and killed in the process and others were wounded," he added.

"Makaluza was lightly wounded in the head in the shootout this morning. He was taken to hospital where he was treated and discharged back to maximum security at St Albans," spokesman Madoda Dywati told Reuters.
State radio said six people were wounded in the attack.
Makaluza, who is serving a 16-year sentence for armed robbery, shot and wounded two warders before taking the five men hostage on Monday.
He was due to appear in the Port Elizabeth high court later this month on charges which include robbery and 10 counts of murder.
